relations.note: The dispute concerns moral praise and blame when outcomes and circumstances escape an agent’s control.

record.card: A multicolor screenprint may use a different stencil for each color. Registration keeps each pass aligned with the same sheet, so separate printed shapes meet as intended. The task concerns the relationship among screen, paper, and successive impressions, beyond making any one stencil correctly.

evidence.locator: Preparing and Printing a Screen; multicolor registration paragraph
evidence.note: Different stencils per color and registration of paper and screen.

record.label: Multicolor screenprint registration
record.learning_takeaway: Keep successive color stencils aligned with one sheet during repeated printing.

relations.note: Registration is the multicolor screenprinting task of maintaining alignment between successive stencils and the receiving sheet.

record.card: Steve Reich’s Music for 18 Musicians layers two kinds of musical time. Pianos and mallet instruments maintain a regular pulse, while voices and winds shape passages around the length of a breath. The resulting swells move against a steady beat rather than replacing it.

evidence.locator: Words from the Composer, printed p.10 / PDF p.11
evidence.note: Reich explicitly contrasts continuous piano/mallet pulse and breath-duration pulsing of voices and winds.

record.label: Music for 18 Musicians
record.learning_takeaway: Hear fixed instrumental pulse against breath-length vocal and wind phrases in Reich’s work.

relations.note: The work provides a concrete comparison of metrical pulse and breathing-shaped phrase duration, two interacting ways of organizing musical time.

record.card: Myrmecochory is seed dispersal by ants, often attracted by a fatty seed appendage called an elaiosome. The partnership is context-dependent: a study of introduced thistle in Argentina found that attracted ants retained most seeds, making the interaction harmful rather than mutually beneficial.

evidence.note: Elaiosomes are lipid-rich ant attractions; in the reported Argentine Carduus–Pheidole study most offered seeds stayed in nests and the measured outcome was antagonistic.

record.label: Myrmecochory
record.learning_takeaway: Connect ant seed transport to lipid-rich elaiosomes while recognizing that ecological context can turn a presumed mutualism harmful.

relations.note: Ants provide the transport in this dispersal pathway, with elaiosomes supplying the attraction; the study tests the consequences of that transport.

record.card: Narrative metalepsis crosses the boundary between telling a story and inhabiting it. A narrator might enter the action, or a fictional character might intrude into the narrator’s world. Such crossings can produce comic or fantastic effects by disturbing levels that the narrative normally keeps separate.

evidence.note: Crossing narrative levels; narrator/character intrusion; comic or fantastic effects.

record.label: Narrative metalepsis
record.learning_takeaway: Notice crossings between the level of telling and the world being told.

relations.note: Metalepsis identifies a particular level-crossing device that literary criticism can distinguish from ordinary narration inside one story world.

record.card: Needle felting turns loose wool into dense felt by repeatedly pushing barbed needles through it. The barbs entangle fibers without weaving. In a museum conservation example, fitted felt plugs on a supporting fabric filled moth holes while matching the surrounding textile’s depth and texture.

evidence.locator: Conservation procedure and needle captions, lines 15–28
evidence.note: The conservator describes barbed-needle entanglement, dense wool plugs, an underlay, and matching the depth/texture of moth-damaged cloth.

record.label: Needle felting
record.learning_takeaway: Explain dry fiber entanglement by barbed needles, including the construction of repair plugs.

relations.note: The conservator uses barbed-needle wool plugs and an underlay to support damaged cloth and replace the missing surface visually.

record.card: A choice can change which future people exist, rather than simply improving the lives of the same people. The nonidentity problem asks how such a choice can wrong someone whose life is worth living if the alternative would have meant that particular person never existed.

evidence.locator: Introduction, person-affecting intuition and worthwhile-life qualification
evidence.note: Identity-affecting choices, person-affecting harm, and the worth-having-life assumption are explicitly discussed.

record.label: Nonidentity problem
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why identity-changing choices complicate claims that a particular future person was made worse off.

relations.note: The entry identifies the puzzle as a problem of population ethics and obligations toward possible future people.

record.card: For many U.S. federal regulations, notice-and-comment rulemaking requires an agency to publish a proposal and let interested people submit written views or evidence. The agency then considers relevant submissions and states the adopted rule’s basis and purpose. Statutory exceptions mean this sequence does not govern every rule.

evidence.note: Notice, written participation, consideration, basis-and-purpose statement, and explicit exceptions are in the statute.

record.label: Notice-and-comment rulemaking
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish public participation in covered US administrative rules from simply announcing the final rule.

relations.note: This procedure governs how U.S. administrative agencies make covered rules, a specific process within administrative law.

record.card: An ordinary generating function encodes a sequence as coefficients of successive powers of a symbol. The coefficient of the squared term stores the third entry when indexing starts at zero. Missing powers mean zero entries, so the pattern preserves position as well as value.

evidence.note: Sequence encoding, zero-based coefficient positions and missing-term zeros.

record.label: Ordinary generating function
record.learning_takeaway: Encode a sequence as coefficients of a formal power series, preserving zero entries through absent powers.

relations.note: The source introduces coefficient-based sequence encoding as a tool of discrete mathematics.

record.card: Orthodox seeds survive drying and freezing, making them suitable for conventional seed-bank storage. This physiological category explains why a dry, cold vault can conserve many species. It does not include every seed: recalcitrant seeds lose viability during the same preparation.

evidence.locator: Cryopreservation discussion and Definitions, lines 8–18 and 42–46
evidence.note: The Definitions section distinguishes orthodox tolerance of drying/freezing from recalcitrant sensitivity, explaining suitability for conventional banking.

record.label: Orthodox seeds
record.learning_takeaway: Connect desiccation and freezing tolerance with conventional long-term seed-bank storage.

relations.note: Editorial preservation bridge: tolerance of both drying and freezing identifies seeds suited to conventional cold storage after collection.

record.card: The inner ear emits faint sounds as its outer hair cells respond to stimulation. A sensitive ear-canal microphone can record these otoacoustic emissions. Normal emissions indicate functioning outer hair cells, yet can coexist with disrupted signaling toward the brain, so they do not establish normal hearing.

evidence.locator: How is auditory neuropathy diagnosed?, lines 37–40
evidence.note: The diagnosis section describes microphone-recorded outer-hair-cell sounds and normal OAE coexisting with an abnormal brainstem response.

record.label: Otoacoustic emissions
record.learning_takeaway: Understand how sounds generated by outer hair cells can test one part of hearing without proving the entire pathway is normal.

relations.note: Editorial diagnostic bridge: emissions measure outer-hair-cell function within hearing, while the brainstem-response comparison shows why one sensory stage cannot represent the whole pathway.

record.card: Tiny calcium-carbonate crystals help the inner ear sense head tilt. In the utricle and saccule, gravity shifts a gelatinous layer weighted by these crystals, bending sensory hairs. This mechanism supplies balance information alongside the semicircular canals, which respond to rotational acceleration.

evidence.note: The vestibular section locates crystal-weighted gelatin and hair cells in utricle/saccule and contrasts their tilt sensing with rotational acceleration in canals.

record.label: Otolith organs and head tilt
record.learning_takeaway: Explain how gravity acting on tiny crystals shifts a gelatinous layer and bends vestibular sensory hairs.

relations.note: Editorial classification: the vestibular sensory system converts gravity-driven displacement of crystal-weighted gelatin into hair-cell signals.

record.card: An overhang arises when a party wins more constituency seats than its proportional vote share would normally provide. Under New Zealand’s 2023 allocation rules, it keeps those extra seats, enlarging Parliament. Other parties retain their allocations, so constituency results can alter the legislature’s final size.

evidence.note: Explains excess electorate wins, no additional list seats, increased size, and unchanged other-party allocations.

record.label: Overhang seats
record.learning_takeaway: Understand the extra seats created when constituency victories exceed a party’s proportional entitlement.

relations.note: Mixed constituency-and-list representation can generate a mismatch between local victories and proportional entitlement; overhang rules resolve that electoral design problem.

record.card: Pando is a quaking-aspen clone in Utah’s Fishlake National Forest. Its many trunks arise through vegetative growth from a shared root system, rather than representing a forest of unrelated seedlings. It makes the difference between a visible tree stem and a clonal individual concrete.

evidence.note: The NPS names Pando in Fishlake National Forest and explains clonal vegetative root growth; stem versus genetic individual is the resulting learning distinction.

record.label: Pando
record.learning_takeaway: Use a named aspen clone to distinguish one genetic individual from its many visible trunks.

relations.note: Pando exemplifies vegetative reproduction: new trunks arise from the clone’s root system rather than from genetically distinct seeds.

record.card: Parker Solar Probe shows why temperature alone does not determine heating. The Sun’s corona is extremely hot but sparse, so relatively few particles transfer energy to the spacecraft. A carbon-composite shield separately protects its body from the Sun’s intense radiation.

evidence.locator: The Science Behind Why It Won’t Melt; The Shield That Protects It
evidence.note: Low particle density versus temperature and carbon-composite radiation shield.

record.label: Parker Solar Probe
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish hot sparse plasma from heat transfer and identify the role of the probe’s radiation shield.

relations.note: Editorial thermal-learning bridge: the probe separates particle temperature, collisional energy transfer and radiative shielding in one engineered case.

record.card: The active layer is ground above permafrost that thaws in summer and freezes again in winter. Its thickness is sensitive to surface insulation. In Denali, removal of vegetation by fire can deepen seasonal thaw until plant cover returns, linking a surface disturbance to underground conditions.

evidence.note: The Denali article defines the seasonal active layer and describes insulating vegetation and post-fire deepening until cover returns.

record.label: Active layer above permafrost
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish annual freeze–thaw in the surface layer from the persistently frozen ground beneath it.

relations.note: Editorial Earth-science placement: annual freezing and thawing are controlled partly by vegetation and insulation above long-lived frozen ground.

record.card: The pie rule lets the second player choose sides after seeing the opening move. In Hex, an overwhelmingly strong first placement may simply be taken over by the opponent. This gives the first player a reason to choose a more balanced opening instead.

evidence.note: The ordinary Hex swap procedure and its effect on opening incentives are explicit.

record.label: Pie rule
record.learning_takeaway: Show why letting the second player swap sides changes the incentive behind the opening move.

relations.note: Swapping ownership after the opening placement changes incentives in alternating board games; Hex provides the inspected implementation.

record.card: PostgreSQL’s Repeatable Read uses a snapshot fixed at the first non-transaction-control statement. Later queries see that snapshot plus their transaction’s own writes, hiding other transactions’ later commits. However, serialization anomalies remain possible: a consistent snapshot alone does not guarantee a one-at-a-time execution history.

evidence.locator: §13.2.2, snapshot timing, own-write exception and serialization warning
evidence.note: PostgreSQL-specific snapshot semantics and remaining anomaly class.

record.label: PostgreSQL Repeatable Read snapshots
record.learning_takeaway: Understand a transaction’s consistent snapshot and why that guarantee alone is weaker than serial execution.

relations.note: This database transaction isolation rule determines which committed row versions are visible during successive reads.

record.card: Projex is a connection game played on a representation of the real projective plane. Players color tiles to form a loop that cannot shrink to a point on that surface. Its spherical display pairs opposite tiles, making an abstract topological identification part of every move.

evidence.note: Defines Projective Hex, noncontractible winning cycles, the antipodal sphere representation, and paired coloring.

record.label: Projex
record.learning_takeaway: Connect winning loops in a projective-plane game to the topology of its board.

relations.note: Players alternately occupy a defined board to meet a connection objective; this makes the named topological game a concrete board-game example.

record.card: A narrative can disclose later events before reaching them. This is prolepsis, or a flashforward. In the Aeneid’s sixth book, the vision of Augustus anticipates a future beyond Aeneas’ own story, linking a character’s present to the later world familiar to the poem’s audience.

evidence.note: Flashforward definition; Aeneid book 6 and Augustus anticipation.

record.label: Prolepsis (narrative)
record.learning_takeaway: Identify an anticipation of later events that interrupts chronological narrative order.

relations.note: Prolepsis names a forward shift that critics use to distinguish narrated order from chronological event order.
The source contrasts forward anticipation with retrospective narration as opposite disruptions of chronological order.

record.card: A single fixed pulley mainly changes the direction of a pull. In an ideal, frictionless pulley system, parallel rope segments supporting the moving load share its weight, reducing the required pull. Counting supporting segments matters more than simply counting pulley wheels.

evidence.note: Fixed-pulley redirection and ideal supporting-segment force multiplication.

record.label: Mechanical advantage in pulley systems
record.learning_takeaway: Understand why a fixed pulley redirects force while several supporting rope segments can multiply it.

relations.note: Editorial mechanical-engineering placement: arranging ropes and sheaves changes the force transmitted to a load, a specific simple-machine design mechanism.

record.card: Pulmonary surfactant is a mixture of lipids and proteins secreted by type II alveolar cells. It lowers surface tension in the fluid lining the lung’s air sacs. By reducing that inward pull, it helps the alveoli stay open during exhalation.

evidence.note: Type II alveolar cells secrete pulmonary surfactant composed of phospholipids and proteins, reducing surface tension.
Surfactant reduces alveolar fluid surface tension and helps prevent air-sac collapse during expiration.

record.label: Pulmonary surfactant
record.learning_takeaway: Connect type II alveolar secretion with lower surface tension and resistance to air-sac collapse.

relations.note: Surfactant lowers the alveolar surface tension that otherwise resists expansion and promotes collapse, a mechanical component of breathing.

record.card: A Python generator function uses yield to return a value while suspending its work. When another value is requested, execution resumes with local variables intact. This packages an iterator’s bookkeeping into the function itself instead of requiring a manually managed state object.

evidence.note: Yield, resumption and automatic preservation of iterator state.

record.label: Python generator functions
record.learning_takeaway: Understand yield as suspension that preserves local variables and execution position until the next request.

relations.note: Generator functions are a Python language construct that implements resumable iteration through yield and saved execution state.

record.card: Python evaluates a function’s default arguments when the definition executes, not on every call. If a default list is mutated, later calls can see the accumulated contents. Using None as the default and creating a list inside the function avoids sharing that default list.

evidence.note: Definition-time evaluation, shared mutable object and fresh-list alternative.

record.label: Mutable default arguments in Python
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why mutations to a default list can persist across function calls, and why a None sentinel changes that behavior.

relations.note: Default-argument evaluation is a language-specific function-definition rule whose shared mutable values affect later Python calls.

record.card: An orbiting planet pulls its star back and forth. Radial-velocity searches detect that motion through periodic shifts in the star’s spectral wavelengths as it approaches and recedes. The method can reveal a planet even when the planet’s own light is not separately seen.

evidence.note: Planetary gravitational tug and alternating wavelength shifts.

record.label: Radial-velocity exoplanet detection
record.learning_takeaway: Infer an unseen planet from periodic spectral shifts caused by the host star’s line-of-sight motion.

relations.note: Editorial classification: the source’s approaching/receding wavelength shifts are the Doppler-effect premise used here to infer stellar motion and an unseen companion.

record.card: Mountains can divide wet landscapes from dry ones. Rising air cools and loses moisture as precipitation on windward slopes; descending air warms and dries on the leeward side. Hawaii’s contrasting green and brown slopes make this rain-shadow mechanism visible in vegetation.

evidence.note: The Hawaii account explains windward cooling/precipitation, leeward warming/drying and the corresponding green/brown vegetation pattern.

record.label: Rain shadow
record.learning_takeaway: Trace orographic rain loss and leeward warming to contrasting vegetation on opposite mountain slopes.

relations.note: Editorial climatic bridge: mountain-forced ascent and descent repeatedly redistribute moisture, shaping wet and dry sides of a regional landscape.

record.card: For an ideal solution, Raoult’s law gives each component’s vapor pressure contribution as its liquid mole fraction times its pure vapor pressure at the same temperature. Adding a nonvolatile solute therefore lowers the solvent’s contribution, connecting mixture composition with the vapor above it.

evidence.locator: Vapor Pressure Lowering, Raoult’s law definition and equation
evidence.note: Ideal-mixture proportionality and nonvolatile-solute consequence.

record.label: Raoult’s law
record.learning_takeaway: Relate each component’s partial vapor pressure to its mole fraction in an ideal solution.

relations.note: The law specifies component vapor pressures above an ideal solution, so it is a property of solution composition and equilibrium.

record.card: Recalcitrant seeds cannot tolerate the drying used in conventional seed banking. Examples include cacao and mango. Their sensitivity motivates alternatives such as preserving excised embryos at extremely low temperatures, but workable cryopreservation methods must be developed rather than assuming every seed can simply be frozen.

evidence.locator: Cryopreservation discussion and Definitions, lines 8–18 and 42–46
evidence.note: Kew describes drying-sensitive seeds, cacao and mango examples, excised-embryo cryopreservation and the need to develop alternative conservation protocols.

record.label: Recalcitrant seeds
record.learning_takeaway: Understand why drying-sensitive seeds cannot use conventional dry-freezer seed banking and motivate alternative preservation research.

relations.note: Editorial preservation bridge: desiccation sensitivity limits which seed-saving storage methods keep the embryo alive and motivates alternatives to dry freezing.

record.card: Failing to recognize a word does not always mean it cannot be recalled. Someone may overlook Shaw in a list of authors yet supply it after “George Bernard.” Recognition failure of recallable words shows that the form of a retrieval cue can change apparent memory success.

evidence.note: The Shaw/George Bernard dissociation and its name are explicitly described.

record.label: Recognition failure of recallable words
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish failing to recognize a word from lacking a retrievable memory of it.

relations.note: The source identifies an experimental dissociation between recognition and cued recall, both methods for measuring memory retrieval.

record.card: A reference group provides a standard people use to judge their behavior or aspirations. It need not be a group they belong to: admired athletes can serve as a comparison point. Several reference groups may send competing messages, making apparent personal preferences partly a matter of social comparison.

evidence.note: Defines comparison standards, athlete examples, multiple groups, and conflicting messages.

record.label: Reference groups
record.learning_takeaway: Separate groups used as comparison standards from groups a person actually belongs to.

relations.note: The sociology chapter treats reference groups as sources of standards and norms used in social comparison.

record.card: Overbending compensates for springback by forming sheet metal beyond its intended final angle, allowing elastic recovery toward the target shape. Its usefulness depends on tooling and part geometry. Comparing angular correction with harder-to-control sidewall curl reveals why one compensation method cannot address every distortion equally.

evidence.note: Supports deliberate angular compensation, tooling/geometry constraints and reduced success for sidewall curl.

record.label: Overbending for springback compensation
record.learning_takeaway: Understand deliberate overbending as a bounded compensation method rather than the springback phenomenon itself.

relations.note: The inspected correction guide explicitly presents overbending as a method of compensating springback.

record.card: A Python list comprehension builds a new list from an expression and one or more iteration clauses, optionally filtering items with conditions. Comparing a comprehension that squares numbers with an equivalent loop reveals how transformation, iteration, and selection fit into one construct.

evidence.note: Section 5.1.3 defines syntax and provides squares, equivalent loop and filtering examples.

record.label: Python list comprehensions
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize the separate transformation, iteration and filtering parts of a Python comprehension.

relations.note: Editorial navigation: This language-specific construct is a facet of Python, not a synonym for the entire language.

record.card: A Python list comprehension builds a new list by applying an expression across one or more iteration clauses, optionally filtering with conditions. The clauses keep their loop-like order, so changing which loop comes first can change the resulting order of combinations.

evidence.note: New-list construction, optional filters and preservation of clause ordering.

record.label: Python list comprehensions
record.learning_takeaway: Combine transformation, iteration and optional filtering into a new list, contrasted with resumable generation.

relations.note: A comprehension is a Python construct that expresses a list-producing loop and optional selection in one expression.
Editorial iteration comparison: list comprehensions produce a completed list, whereas generator functions preserve execution state between requested values.

record.card: Springback in sheet-metal bending is the change in shape caused by elastic recovery after forming loads are removed. Permanent deformation remains, but the final angle can differ from the tool’s angle. Exploring unloading on a stress–strain curve separates elastic recovery from plastic shaping.

evidence.note: Supports unloading, elastic recovery, remaining plastic shape, angular deviation and stress–strain explanation.

record.label: Springback in sheet-metal bending
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish elastic recovery during unloading from the permanent bend.

relations.note: Editorial connection between the selected learning takeaways, not a source-asserted hierarchy.

record.card: Retrieving some memories can make related, unpracticed memories harder to recall. In Anderson and colleagues’ word-category experiments, participants practiced selected items, then recalled fewer unpracticed members of those categories on a later test. Measuring only practiced items can therefore miss other effects of the exercise.

evidence.note: The category practice design and delayed impairment of unpracticed related items establish the phenomenon.

record.label: Retrieval-induced forgetting
record.learning_takeaway: Understand how practicing retrieval of selected items can impair recall of related unpracticed items.

relations.note: The experiment concerns long-term memory retrieval and selective later forgetting of related representations.

record.card: A rhumb line keeps a constant course. On a Mercator chart it appears straight, so a navigator can measure its angle against the meridians to determine a steering direction. This links a projection’s geometry to the practical task of following a course at sea.

evidence.locator: Map Projections: Mercator and rhumb lines
evidence.note: Constant course, straight Mercator representation and meridian-angle measurement.

record.label: Rhumb line
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why a straight Mercator-chart line is convenient for maintaining a constant course.

relations.note: A constant-course line becomes a practical navigation tool because Mercator charts allow its steering direction to be measured directly.

record.card: Rhythmic augmentation lengthens a musical idea’s note values, commonly doubling every duration. A motive written in quarter notes can return in half notes while preserving its relative rhythm. The technique expands the idea in time rather than adding extra notes to extend the phrase.

evidence.locator: §11.2.3, definition and Bach Invention No.1 example
evidence.note: Defines usual doubling of durations and illustrates augmentation of a contrapuntal motive.

record.label: Rhythmic augmentation
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize proportionally lengthened note values while the motive remains identifiable.

relations.note: Proportional expansion of note durations is a particular transformation of rhythmic organization; the Bach example supplies a compositional use.

record.card: Role conflict occurs when expectations attached to different social roles clash. A person’s responsibilities as an employee may demand staying late while responsibilities as a parent require leaving. The problem comes from incompatible roles, even when either role alone would be manageable.

evidence.note: The employee/parent example distinguishes contradictory roles from demands within one role.

record.label: Role conflict
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish incompatible demands across different social roles from pressure within one role.

relations.note: The sociology chapter locates role conflict in the expected behavior associated with multiple social statuses.

record.card: Role strain is pressure from the many demands within a single social role. Parenting, for example, can combine practical work, problem-solving, and moral guidance. This differs from role conflict, where obligations tied to separate roles pull against one another; one role alone can be demanding enough.

evidence.note: Defines too much required of a single role and contrasts contradictory roles, with parenting tasks as illustration.

record.label: Role strain
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize competing demands within a single role even without a clash between separate roles.

relations.note: Role strain is presented as a sociological consequence of demands attached to one social role.

record.card: The Sainte-Laguë method turns party votes into seats by dividing each eligible party’s total by successive odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, and onward. The highest resulting quotients receive seats. Each selected quotient contributes another seat, making the rounding procedure explicit rather than leaving fractional seats unresolved.

evidence.note: Odd divisors, ranking quotients, and counting each party’s selected quotients establish the allocation algorithm.

record.label: Sainte-Laguë method
record.learning_takeaway: Allocate seats by ranking party-vote totals divided by successive odd numbers.

relations.note: A democracy using proportional representation needs a rule for converting vote shares to whole seats; this is one documented allocation method.

record.card: An impermeable seed coat can keep a living embryo from germinating. Scarification deliberately weakens or breaches that covering so water can enter. For Kentucky coffeetree, abrasion provides one route; the treatment addresses a physical barrier rather than every possible cause of dormancy.

evidence.note: The impermeable-coat discussion describes Kentucky coffeetree and abrasion that permits water uptake, distinct from embryo dormancy.

record.label: Seed scarification
record.learning_takeaway: Explain how breaching an impermeable seed coat permits water entry, addressing a different barrier from internal dormancy.

relations.note: Editorial placement: scarification acts on the seed covering’s permeability, connecting seed anatomy to propagation practice.

record.card: Serializable snapshot isolation adds conflict checks to snapshot-based database transactions. PostgreSQL uses these checks to ensure committed serializable transactions could have run one after another. A transaction may instead fail with a serialization error, requiring the application to retry its work.

evidence.locator: §13.2.3, serializability guarantee, anomaly detection and implementation name
evidence.note: SSI checks, committed-result guarantee and serialization retries.

record.label: Serializable snapshot isolation
record.learning_takeaway: Combine snapshot reads with checks that abort unsafe concurrent transactions so successful results can match a serial order.

relations.note: Serializable snapshot isolation is the database concurrency-control technique identified for PostgreSQL’s Serializable transactions.
The documentation says SSI builds on snapshot isolation by adding anomaly checks, unlike Repeatable Read’s snapshot guarantee alone.

record.card: Some plants retain mature seeds instead of releasing them immediately. In serotinous lodgepole-pine cones, resin seals can hold seeds for years until heat opens the cone. After fire, an open canopy and cleared ground can favor the released seedlings.

evidence.note: Resin-sealed lodgepole cones retain seeds for years; heat opens them, and the ensuing light and cleared ground favor establishment.

record.label: Serotiny
record.learning_takeaway: Explain delayed cone opening through resin seals and the post-fire conditions favoring seedling establishment.

relations.note: Retaining seeds in sealed cones changes the timing of seed dispersal; the lodgepole example releases them when fire opens the canopy.

record.card: FIDE’s 2023 seventy-five-move rule automatically draws a chess game after 75 moves by each player without a pawn move or capture. Counting both players’ moves matters. If the final move delivers checkmate, however, that result takes precedence over this automatic draw.

evidence.note: The rule gives the per-player count, both resetting events, automatic intervention, and checkmate exception.

record.label: Seventy-five-move rule
record.learning_takeaway: Understand an automatic draw after 75 moves by each player without pawn moves or captures, with checkmate taking precedence.

relations.note: This rule limits a chess game’s continuation using a counter reset by pawn moves or captures, with an explicit checkmate exception.

record.card: At Ise Jingu, Shikinen Sengu follows a twenty-year renewal cycle. A new sanctuary is built on an adjacent alternate site, and sacred furnishings are remade before the divine symbol is transferred. Continuity here depends on repeating forms and rituals while replacing the buildings’ material fabric.

evidence.note: Twenty-year cycle, alternate site, renewed furnishings and transfer ritual.

record.label: Shikinen Sengu at Ise
record.learning_takeaway: Understand continuity maintained through periodic rebuilding and transfer rather than unchanged fabric.

relations.note: Ise’s renewal culminates in transferring the sacred symbol within a continuing Shinto ritual cycle.
The rebuilding practice offers a specific comparison between continuity of sacred architectural form and preservation of original building fabric.

record.card: A pulse oximeter estimates blood oxygen saturation using light. Skin pigmentation can affect its accuracy, and the FDA highlights concerns about poorer performance in darker skin. Circulation, skin temperature, and nail polish can also alter readings, making the displayed number an estimate with limitations.

evidence.locator: Opening explanation; FDA Efforts; February 2021 Safety Communication, lines 83, 97–131
evidence.note: The page explains optical oxygen estimates, FDA concern about darker-skin accuracy, and circulation, temperature and nail-polish effects.

record.label: Skin pigmentation and pulse oximetry
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why an optical oxygen estimate can have skin-pigmentation-dependent error and cannot be treated as an infallible reading.

relations.note: Editorial clinical bridge: interpreting an optical oxygen measurement requires accounting for pigmentation and other sources of device error.

record.card: Oral rehydration exploits coupled absorption of sodium and glucose in the intestine; water follows the resulting osmotic gradient. This transport pathway can keep working during severe diarrhea. More concentrated mixtures are not automatically better, because excessive solute concentration can impair net water absorption.

evidence.locator: Scientific Basis for Oral Rehydration Therapy, lines 46–49
evidence.note: The transport discussion supports sodium–glucose coupling, passive osmotic water movement, preserved function in diarrhea, and problems from high osmolarity.

record.label: Sodium–glucose cotransport in oral rehydration
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why glucose and sodium together promote intestinal water absorption during diarrhea.

relations.note: Editorial clinical bridge: formulated oral rehydration uses preserved intestinal sodium–glucose transport to restore fluid absorption during diarrheal illness.

record.card: A spanning tree keeps every vertex of a finite connected graph while discarding enough edges to eliminate cycles. Removing an edge from a cycle leaves an alternate connection. Repeating that step produces a connected, cycle-free backbone, though different choices can produce different spanning trees.

evidence.note: All-vertex tree subgraph and cycle-edge deletion algorithm.

record.label: Spanning tree
record.learning_takeaway: Retain every vertex and connectivity while removing cyclic redundancy from a graph.

relations.note: A spanning tree is a subgraph preserving the original graph’s vertices and connectivity while removing cycles.

record.card: Stable sorting preserves the previous order of records with equal keys. That permits multi-pass sorting: order records by the secondary key first, then stably sort by the primary key. Ties in the final pass retain the secondary ordering established earlier.

evidence.note: Tie-order preservation and secondary-before-primary pass order.

record.label: Stable multi-pass sorting
record.learning_takeaway: Sort by a secondary key before a primary key because stable sorts preserve earlier order among ties.

relations.note: Editorial algorithmic placement: composition of stable sorting passes implements lexicographic key priority through a preserved-order invariant.

record.card: Stratified sortition combines chance with demographic balancing when recruiting a citizens’ assembly. Ireland first invites randomly selected households, then selects among applicants so the group broadly reflects characteristics such as age, gender, and geography. Random invitations alone would not perform this second balancing step.

evidence.note: The current recruitment account separates random household invitation from stratified selection using demographic information.

record.label: Stratified sortition for citizens’ assemblies
record.learning_takeaway: Combine random invitations with demographic balancing rather than treating volunteers as a representative sample.

relations.note: The official assembly FAQ identifies this two-stage procedure as its method of selecting citizen members.

record.card: In “I saw the person with the telescope,” the telescope might belong to the person or be the instrument of seeing. Structural ambiguity comes from different ways of grouping the same words. It differs from ambiguity caused by a single word having several meanings.

evidence.locator: Structural ambiguity: Hilary/pirate/telescope example; lexical ambiguity contrast
evidence.note: Alternative prepositional-phrase attachments; structural versus lexical ambiguity.

record.label: Structural ambiguity
record.learning_takeaway: Identify alternative phrase attachments that change meaning without changing word senses.

relations.note: Alternative phrase attachments offer linguistic evidence that sentence structure contributes to meaning beyond individual word senses.
Constituency diagnostics help test the competing phrase groupings that produce a structurally ambiguous reading.

record.card: Structural holes are gaps between otherwise disconnected social groups. A person spanning such a gap can encounter contrasting ideas and broker information between groups. Burt’s account focuses on the network position that makes combining perspectives possible when opinion and behavior are more similar within groups than between them.

evidence.locator: Abstract and opening argument, original pp.349–350
evidence.note: Contrasts within-group similarity and between-group differences and states the brokerage/synthesis mechanism.

record.label: Structural holes
record.learning_takeaway: Identify brokerage opportunities where otherwise disconnected groups hold different information.

relations.note: The paper defines brokerage across gaps between groups as a structural property of social networks.

record.card: Beyond its critical temperature and pressure, a substance forms a supercritical fluid without a separate liquid–gas boundary. Such fluids can penetrate small pores while dissolving materials. Supercritical carbon dioxide, for example, can extract caffeine from coffee and then be removed by lowering pressure.

evidence.locator: Supercritical Fluids, definition and carbon-dioxide extraction example
evidence.note: Critical regime, penetration, solvent action and pressure-release recovery.

record.label: Supercritical fluid
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize the single fluid beyond critical temperature and pressure, with useful solvent properties but no liquid–gas boundary.

relations.note: Editorial placement in thermodynamics: the critical-temperature and pressure regime changes phase boundaries, density and solvent behavior.

record.card: Creating more liquid surface costs energy because molecules there have different surroundings from molecules inside. Surface tension therefore favors smaller surface area: tiny free droplets tend toward spheres, while gravity and contact with surfaces can distort larger drops.

evidence.locator: Cohesive forces and surface tension, Figure 10.16
evidence.note: Surface-energy cost and qualified droplet-shape example.

record.label: Surface tension
record.learning_takeaway: Connect surface free-energy cost with the tendency of small liquid drops to minimize exposed area.

relations.note: Surface tension is a liquid’s interfacial property; cohesive molecular interactions make enlarging the exposed surface energetically costly.

record.card: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault stores backup copies of genebank seeds at minus 18°C. Under its sealed-box arrangement, depositors retain ownership and alone can request their seeds back. The design combines physical preservation with clear custody, protecting collections without transferring control over them.

evidence.locator: Our Purpose; Seed Vault Operations; Facility management, lines 28–38, 45–60
evidence.note: The official page gives duplicate backup storage, minus 18°C conditions, unopened containers, depositor ownership and depositor-only return requests.

record.label: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
record.learning_takeaway: Understand backup seed storage as custodial safety duplication whose deposits stay under the depositor’s control.

relations.note: The vault explicitly serves as a safety depository for orthodox seeds, using dry, cold storage for backup duplicates.

record.card: A swim bladder is a gas-filled pouch that helps many bony fishes regulate buoyancy. Its gases often exchange directly with the blood. Adjusting this gas changes support in water, a different job from extracting oxygen through the gills.

evidence.note: The bony-fish passage describes a gas-filled gut-derived pouch controlling buoyancy, frequent blood gas exchange, and separate gill breathing.

record.label: Swim-bladder buoyancy regulation
record.learning_takeaway: Relate a bony fish’s gas-filled swim bladder and gas exchange with blood to buoyancy control.

relations.note: Editorial placement: the gas-filled swim bladder illustrates how the form and connections of an internal organ enable buoyancy regulation.

record.card: Tawaf is the ritual of circling the Kaaba seven times counterclockwise. In Hajj, the shared movement expresses devotion and communal unity. It differs from Sa’i, the separate passage between Safa and Marwah, so similar-looking crowds may be performing distinct acts within the larger pilgrimage.

evidence.locator: Circumambulation of the Kaaba; Safa and Marwah
evidence.note: Seven counterclockwise circuits; symbolic meaning; distinction from Sa’i.

record.label: Tawaf
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish circling the Kaaba from the separate passage between Safa and Marwah.

relations.note: Tawaf is a specified circling ritual in the Hajj sequence, distinct from its other movements and stations.

record.card: A terminus post quem is an earliest possible date. For an undisturbed archaeological deposit, a coin minted in 1850 would rule out burial before 1850. It would not prove burial during that year: the object could have circulated before entering the ground.

evidence.note: TPQ lower-bound rule; hypothetical coin applies that rule.

record.label: Terminus post quem
record.learning_takeaway: Separate an earliest possible deposition date from an exact date.

relations.note: Archaeologists use the latest eligible artifact date to constrain when a deposit could first have formed.

aliases: The Market for Lemons: Quality Uncertainty and the Market Mechanism
record.card: George Akerlof’s 1970 paper The Market for Lemons uses used cars to model hidden quality. If buyers cannot distinguish good cars from bad ones, the price they offer can discourage owners of good cars from selling, worsening the quality available for trade.

evidence.locator: Original pp.488–489, Introduction and II.A; PDF pp.2–3
evidence.note: Title, authorship, year, illustrative automobile market, asymmetric knowledge, and withdrawal of good cars are established on the inspected pages.

record.label: The Market for Lemons
record.learning_takeaway: Read Akerlof’s used-car model as a mechanism by which hidden quality can drive good products out of trade.

relations.note: Akerlof explicitly models sellers knowing car quality better than buyers and shows how this asymmetric information affects which cars trade.

record.card: Thermokarst develops when thawing ground ice lets the land surface subside. Water may collect in the resulting depressions. Continued thaw does not always enlarge these lakes: if a bank is breached, a lake can drain abruptly, leaving a very different landscape.

evidence.note: The thermokarst section describes ground-ice thaw, subsidence, water-filled depressions and possible abrupt drainage after a breach.

record.label: Thermokarst
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why ground-ice thaw can both create lake basins and cause existing lakes to drain.

relations.note: Editorial Earth-science placement: melting subsurface ice changes ground elevation and drainage, connecting frozen-ground physics with landform evolution.

record.card: Tissot’s indicatrix makes local map distortion visible with projected circles and ellipses. On a conformal map the markers stay circular but can change size; on an equal-area map their areas remain equal while shapes change. Repeating the markers shows how distortion varies from place to place.

evidence.locator: Opening explanation; conformal and equal-area comparisons
evidence.note: Local ellipses; conformal circles; equal-area markers; spatial variation.

record.label: Tissot’s indicatrix
record.learning_takeaway: Read projected ellipses as local evidence of angle and area distortion.

relations.note: Indicatrices visualize the local scale, angular and areal distortions introduced by a map projection.

record.card: Catfacing leaves tomatoes misshapen, with corky scars and sometimes deep cavities near the blossom end. Its causes are not fully established; cold and disturbances to developing flowers are implicated. Large-fruited varieties are often more susceptible, making this a developmental disorder distinct from blossom-end rot.

evidence.note: Catfacing is malformed scarred fruit with possible cavities; the source leaves causes uncertain and implicates cold and floral disturbance, with larger varieties more prone.

record.label: Tomato catfacing
record.learning_takeaway: Identify malformation and scarring associated with disturbed flower development while preserving uncertainty about its causes.

relations.note: Editorial gardening bridge: malformed scarred fruit can trace to flower-development conditions and variety susceptibility, a different cultivation problem from nutrient delivery.

record.card: Tonicization makes a chord other than the home chord behave as a local tonal goal. A secondary dominant approaches that chord as its own dominant would. In C major, D7 can lead strongly to G, temporarily giving the G chord a special sense of arrival.

evidence.note: Defines treating a non-I chord as tonic and identifies D7 as V/V progressing to G in C major.

record.label: Tonicization
record.learning_takeaway: Hear a secondary dominant make a non-tonic chord a temporary harmonic goal.

relations.note: Secondary-dominant motion changes the local function of a chord within a harmonic progression; harmony is the broader organizing subject.

record.card: Tree-ring crossdating matches patterns of wide and narrow rings across different trees. Overlapping sequences from living trees and older preserved wood can extend a chronology beyond one tree’s lifetime, anchoring archaeological samples to calendar years rather than merely counting their rings.

evidence.locator: Dendrochronology: The Study of Tree Rings; paragraphs on annual rings and crossdating
evidence.note: Pattern matching among living and preserved trees extends chronologies.

record.label: Tree-ring crossdating
record.learning_takeaway: Match overlapping ring-width patterns to place wood on a calendar chronology.

relations.note: Crossdating is the ring-pattern matching procedure that links samples into a dendrochronological chronology.

record.card: Kidneys partly regulate filtration by sampling their own tubular fluid. Macula densa cells detect increased flow and salt delivery, then local signals narrow the incoming arteriole and reduce filtration. This tubuloglomerular feedback links downstream sensing to the blood supply feeding the same filtering unit.

evidence.note: The tubuloglomerular section links increased tubular flow/salt with macula densa signaling, afferent constriction and reduced filtration.

record.label: Tubuloglomerular feedback
record.learning_takeaway: Trace macula densa sensing to local afferent-arteriole adjustment that opposes changes in kidney filtration.

relations.note: Editorial feedback classification: downstream salt/flow sensing changes the incoming arteriole so filtration moves back toward its regulated level.

record.card: A turbofan sends some air through its combustion core and some around it. Bypass ratio compares those two mass-flow rates, with bypass flow in the numerator. The bypass stream still contributes thrust, so propulsion does not require burning fuel in every parcel of accelerated air.

evidence.locator: Fan flow; bypass ratio definition; combined thrust explanation
evidence.note: Definition and distinct thrust contributions of bypass and core streams.

record.label: Turbofan bypass ratio
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish bypass air from engine-core flow and compare their mass-flow rates.

relations.note: Editorial aerospace-engineering placement: bypass-to-core mass flow is a propulsion-design parameter controlling how the fan and core contribute thrust.

record.card: The Universal Transverse Mercator system locates points within sixty zones, normally six degrees of longitude wide. Its plane-coordinate grids offer an alternative to latitude and longitude. Choosing UTM can make certain maps easier to use, but the notation is not inherently more accurate than geographic coordinates.

evidence.note: Sixty-zone plane grid and no inherent accuracy advantage over latitude/longitude.

record.label: Universal Transverse Mercator grid
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize zone-based planar coordinates as an alternative position notation, not inherently greater accuracy.

relations.note: UTM supplies a zone-based plane coordinate framework that cartographers can place on maps to identify locations.

record.card: An unreliable narrator need not lie about what happened. A narrator may report events accurately yet misunderstand them or judge them in ways the text undermines. Critics therefore distinguish reporting, interpreting, and evaluating, using clues such as contradictions within the account or clashes with other characters.

evidence.locator: Definition; Explication; Features and Causes of Unreliability
evidence.note: Three narratorial functions; accurate reporting with unreliable interpretation; textual clues.

record.label: Unreliable narration
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish factual reporting from interpretation and evaluation when assessing a narrator.

relations.note: This distinction structures critical reading of gaps between a narrator’s account and the implications of the surrounding text.

record.card: A winter chill can prepare a plant to flower later. This response, vernalization, is obligatory in some herbaceous perennials and merely improves flowering in others. Some plants must first pass a juvenile stage, so cold exposure alone does not guarantee bloom.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraphs and Juvenility Issues, lines 29–32
evidence.note: The article distinguishes obligatory and facultative cold responses for flowering and notes that some perennials must mature first.

record.label: Vernalization
record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish cold exposure needed or helpful for flowering from cold treatments that break seed dormancy.

relations.note: Editorial classification: a cold requirement controls entry into flowering, one stage of plant sexual reproduction; it is not the same trigger as seed germination.

record.card: Virginia Apgar turned observations familiar from anesthesia into a rapid assessment of newborn condition. Her system considered heart rate, breathing, reflex response, muscle tone, and color. A fixed set of signs made the first moments after birth easier to assess systematically across babies.

evidence.note: The NLM history identifies Apgar’s adaptation of anesthesia signs and lists heart rate, respiration, reflex irritability, muscle tone and color.

record.label: Virginia Apgar
record.learning_takeaway: Understand how Apgar transferred five anesthesia observations into a rapid standardized newborn assessment.

relations.note: Editorial historical bridge: Apgar transferred monitored physiological signs into a repeatable newborn assessment, linking anesthesiology to early neonatal care.

record.card: Voyager 2 visited Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune by following a carefully arranged sequence of planetary encounters. Gravity assists at successive worlds redirected and boosted its Sun-relative motion, turning a launch aimed toward Jupiter into a tour of all four giant planets.

evidence.note: Four giant-planet flybys and mission extension.
Successive boosts and launch energy initially sufficient for Jupiter.

record.label: Voyager 2
record.learning_takeaway: Learn how gravity-assist mission design extended one probe’s journey to all four giant planets.

relations.note: Voyager 2 explicitly used Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus encounters to change its trajectory and reach subsequent giant planets.

record.card: Weak ties are casual connections rather than close relationships. Granovetter’s explanation emphasizes their reach: an acquaintance can connect someone to a social circle beyond their usual contacts, bringing different information or opportunities. Their value depends on that position in the network, not simply on having many acquaintances.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion and Granovetter interview quotation
evidence.note: Defines casual connections and explains access to networks outside one’s own circle.

record.label: Weak ties
record.learning_takeaway: Explain why casual acquaintances can supply information beyond one’s close circle.

relations.note: Granovetter explicitly explains weak ties through the different social circles they connect within a network.

record.card: A woodcut is made by removing wood around the lines and shapes meant to print. Ink sits on the surviving raised surface. Because movable type also prints in relief, woodblocks could be placed beside type and printed together, helping integrate illustrations with text in early books.

evidence.note: Relief image, removal of nonprinting wood, and printing alongside type.

record.label: Woodcut
record.learning_takeaway: Recognize why uncut raised wood prints the image and can share a press with type.

relations.note: Woodcut is a relief process in which the raised parts of a carved woodblock transfer ink to paper.
